lineage: Assessed by Sophos as tied to BlackSuit/Royal (ex-Conti) and to BlackBasta-affiliated vishing actors (STAC5777)
summary: 3AM first appeared in 2023 when Symantec saw an affiliate fall back to it after LockBit was blocked; that intrusion used gpresult, Cobalt Strike, PsExec, account creation and Wput FTP exfiltration before stopping security/backup services and deleting shadow copies (.threeamtime). In 2025 Sophos documented 3AM affiliates combining email bombing with spoofed-IT vishing to obtain Microsoft Quick Assist sessions, then running a hidden QEMU virtual machine with the QDoor backdoor, WMIC/PowerShell execution, a local 'SupportUser' admin account, XEOX RMM, extensive native discovery, EDR-killer attempts and GoodSync exfiltration of ~868 GB to Backblaze.
uniqueTraits: Email bombing followed by phone vishing that spoofs the victim's own IT department number
Microsoft Quick Assist for hands-on initial access
QEMU-hosted Windows 7 VM carrying the QDoor backdoor to hide from endpoint protection (T1564.006)
XEOX and Syncro RMM for persistence; GoodSync to Backblaze for large-scale exfiltration
Scheduled task named 'WindowsSensor15' (Conti playbook) and EDR killer attempts
Used as a fallback encryptor when LockBit deployment was blocked (Wput FTP exfil, .threeamtime)

sources.title: A familiar playbook with a twist: 3AM ransomware actors dropped virtual machine with vishing and Quick Assist
3AM: New Ransomware Family Used As Fallback in Failed LockBit Attack

chain.procedure: Target inboxes are flooded via mailing-list subscriptions (24 emails in 3 minutes), then a VoIP call spoofing the internal IT number persuades the employee to grant remote access.
chain.noAtomicReason: Email bombing and vishing are social-engineering steps outside the endpoint; no local Atomic Red Team test applies. Validate with mail-flow anomaly and helpdesk-call procedures.

chain.procedure: The victim launches Microsoft Quick Assist and hands the session to the caller.

atomics.testName: Microsoft App Quick Assist Execution
atomics.note: [T1219] Microsoft Quick Assist execution.

chain.procedure: Via the victim's Chrome session, the actor visits a lookalike msquick[.]link domain that redirects to a Google Drive archive (UpdatePackage_excic.zip) extracted to C:\ProgramData.

atomics.testName: Windows - PowerShell Download
atomics.note: [T1105] PowerShell download of a remote archive.

atomics.testName: Malware Masquerading and Execution from Zip File
atomics.note: [T1036] Execution from a downloaded ZIP masquerading as an update.

chain.procedure: A VBS script launches a portable QEMU Windows 7 VM bridged to the host network; no install or admin rights needed, invisible to the host EDR.

atomics.testName: Create and start VirtualBox virtual machine
atomics.note: [T1564.006] Creates and starts a VirtualBox VM (different hypervisor, same evasion).

atomics.testName: Visual Basic script execution to gather local computer information
atomics.note: [T1059.005] VBScript execution, as used to launch the VM.

chain.procedure: The pre-installed QDoor backdoor inside the VM connects to a hard-coded C2 IP on TCP/443; Quick Assist is then closed.

atomics.testName: Powercat C2
atomics.note: [T1095] Raw TCP reverse channel (powercat) as a stand-in for QDoor.

chain.procedure: WMIC is used to run PowerShell on a server, and later to move to nine further hosts.

atomics.testName: WMI Execute Remote Process
atomics.note: [T1047] WMI remote process execution.

atomics.testName: Create a Process using WMI Query and an Encoded Command
atomics.note: [T1047] WMI process creation with encoded PowerShell.

chain.procedure: Creates local account 'SupportUser' and adds it to the local Administrators group, then logs on over RDP; Symantec also saw a new user added for persistence in 2023.

atomics.testName: Create a new Windows admin user
atomics.note: [T1136.001] Creates a new Windows admin user.

chain.procedure: Installs XEOX remote-management (cloud portal) and later Syncro Live Agent for persistent access.

atomics.testName: MSP360 Connect Execution
atomics.note: [T1219] Cloud RMM agent execution; no XEOX/Syncro-specific atomic exists.

atomics.testName: ScreenConnect Application Download and Install on Windows
atomics.note: [T1219] RMM application download and install.

chain.procedure: Runs gpresult to dump policy settings for a user (first activity in the 2023 intrusion).

atomics.testName: Display group policy information via gpresult
atomics.note: [T1615] gpresult group policy discovery.

chain.procedure: nltest used to list domain trusts and domain controllers, alongside whoami /all, net group "Domain Admins", net sessions, quser, wmic product, ipconfig /all, netstat and ping sweeps; output saved to pc.txt/dir.txt/a1.txt.

atomics.testName: Windows - Discover domain trusts with nltest
atomics.note: [T1482] Domain trust discovery with nltest.

atomics.testName: Elevated group enumeration using net group (Domain)
atomics.note: [T1069.002] net group enumeration of Domain Admins.

atomics.testName: System Network Connections Discovery
atomics.note: [T1049] netstat / net session network connection discovery.

chain.procedure: Moves with a compromised domain admin via RDP, remote PowerShell, WMIC and XEOX; a d.bat file enables RDP and opens a firewall port on targets.

atomics.testName: Enable RDP via Registry (fDenyTSConnections)
atomics.note: [T1112] Enables RDP via fDenyTSConnections registry change.

atomics.testName: Allow SMB and RDP on Microsoft Defender Firewall
atomics.note: [T1686] Allows SMB and RDP through the Windows firewall.

atomics.testName: Remote Code Execution with PS Credentials Using Invoke-Command
atomics.note: [T1021.006] Remote PowerShell execution with Invoke-Command.

chain.techniqueName: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
chain.procedure: Attempts to remove Duo MFA via WMIC, a SYSTEM scheduled task named 'WindowsSensor15' and msiexec, and runs an EDR killer (EDR Sandblaster); 3AM itself stops security services before encryption.

atomics.testName: Stop and Remove Arbitrary Security Windows Service
atomics.note: [T1685] Stops and removes a security service.

atomics.testName: Kill antimalware protected processes using Backstab
atomics.note: [T1685] Kills protected AV processes via a vulnerable-driver tool (Backstab).

atomics.testName: Scheduled task Local
atomics.note: [T1053.005] Scheduled task creation as used for the 'WindowsSensor15' task.

chain.techniqueName: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
chain.procedure: GoodSync installed on two hosts uploads ~868 GB to Backblaze cloud storage.

atomics.testName: Exfiltrate data with rclone to cloud Storage - Mega (Windows)
atomics.note: [T1567.002] Sync-tool (rclone) exfiltration to cloud storage.

chain.procedure: Wput used to exfiltrate victim files to an attacker-controlled FTP server.

atomics.testName: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol - FTP - Rclone
atomics.note: [T1048.003] FTP exfiltration with a command-line client (rclone).

chain.procedure: PsExec used to escalate/execute remotely; on Day 9 C:\L.exe and 1.bat target 88 computers through C$ admin shares.

atomics.testName: Use PsExec to execute a command on a remote host
atomics.note: [T1569.002] PsExec remote execution.

atomics.testName: Map admin share
atomics.note: [T1021.002] Maps the C$ admin share.

chain.procedure: Stops services of security and backup products (Veeam, Acronis, Ivanti, McAfee, Symantec) before encryption.

atomics.testName: Windows - Stop service using net.exe
atomics.note: [T1489] Stops services with net.exe.

atomics.testName: Windows - Stop service using Service Controller
atomics.note: [T1489] Stops services with sc.exe.

chain.procedure: Deletes Volume Shadow Copies after encryption.

atomics.testName: Windows - Delete Volume Shadow Copies
atomics.note: [T1490] vssadmin delete shadows.

chain.procedure: Encrypts files appending .threeamtime; in 2025 encryption was largely blocked except on the unprotected server, but data had already been stolen.

atomics.testName: PureLocker Ransom Note
atomics.note: [T1486] Ransom-note drop simulation (non-encrypting).
